questions.def: "Less" is used for uncountable nouns in comparative statements.
questions.question: This research is ___ comprehensive than the previous study.

questions.def: "Most" forms the superlative of multi-syllable adjectives.
questions.question: Of all the candidates, she presented the ___ reasoned argument.

questions.def: "Best" is the superlative form of the adjective "good".
questions.question: This is the ___ coffee I've ever tasted.

questions.def: "The more... the more" structure for parallel increase.
questions.question: The ___ we invest in education, the brighter our future.

questions.def: "Most" is used to form the superlative with longer adjectives.
questions.question: He is by far the ___ experienced candidate for the job.

questions.def: "Worse" is the comparative form of the adjective "bad".
questions.question: This year's results are ___ than last year's.

questions.def: "Far" intensifies comparatives, emphasizing the difference.
questions.question: The situation is ___ complex than I initially thought.

questions.def: "By far" emphasizes the superlative quality.
questions.question: This is ___ the most interesting book I've read this year.

questions.def: "Easier" is the comparative form of the adjective "easy".
questions.question: This exercise is ___ than the previous one.

questions.def: With two options, use the comparative, "more appealing".
questions.question: Of the two options, this one seems ___ appealing.

questions.def: "The more... the safer" structure for parallel consequence.
questions.question: The ___ people are vaccinated, the safer everyone will be.

questions.def: "Less" is the correct comparative form of "little" for uncountable nouns.
questions.question: He showed ___ concern than I expected.

questions.def: "Less" is used for uncountable nouns like "time" in comparisons.
questions.question: The ___ time you spend planning, the greater the risk of failure.

questions.def: "More than willing" is an idiom meaning very willing.
questions.question: He is ___ than willing to help with the project.

questions.def: "Farthest" is the superlative form of "far" related to distance.
questions.question: This is the ___ I've ever travelled.

questions.def: "Longer" is the comparative of "long", indicating duration.
questions.question: The ___ you wait, the worse it will get.

questions.def: "Most" forms the superlative of multi-syllable adjectives.
questions.question: This is the ___ recent news on the subject.

questions.def: "Latest" is the superlative form of "late" referring to time.
questions.question: This is the ___ I've ever stayed up.

questions.def: "Less" is for uncountable nouns, indicating smaller amount.
questions.question: The ___ you know, the better.

questions.def: "By far" emphasizes the superlative degree.
questions.question: She is by ___ the smartest person I know.

questions.def: "Nearest" is the superlative form of "near", indicating proximity.
questions.question: This is the ___ airport to the city center.

questions.def: "The more... the happier" structure for parallel increase.
questions.question: The ___ I see him, the happier I become.

questions.def: "Without doubt" intensifies the superlative expression.
questions.question: This is without ___ the most beautiful place I've seen.

questions.def: 'Less' is the correct comparative form for uncountable nouns like insight.
questions.question: This research is ___ insightful than her previous work.

questions.def: Use 'the most' for superlatives with adjectives of three or more syllables.
questions.question: Of all the candidates, she is ___ qualified.

questions.def: 'Better' is the irregular comparative form of the adjective 'good'.
questions.question: His latest novel is ___ than his first.

questions.def: The correlative construction 'the more, the brighter' requires 'more'.
questions.question: The ___ we invest in education, the brighter our future.

questions.def: 'By far' is used to emphasize a superlative adjective.
questions.question: This is by ___ the most impressive presentation I've seen.

questions.def: 'Later' is the correct comparative for time when comparing two things.
questions.question: Of the two proposals, this one arrived ___.

questions.def: 'More' is the standard comparative form for adjectives like 'intelligent'.
questions.question: She is ___ intelligent than I initially thought.
